superseded_snapshot.status_on_site: Kept as a dated historical snapshot in data/snapshots; the 11/15 report is one day old and covers the 11/15-11/16 slates. This 11/16 file supersedes it for the 11/16-11/17 slates.

supersession_note: This is one dated snapshot, not the newest possible report. The league publishes updated reports on a continual basis (the index lists 11/16 reports every 15 minutes), and any later file supersedes it.
extraction_notes: Game Time in the PDF is a 12-hour clock with no AM/PM marker (e.g. "07:00 (ET)"). Meridiems in tip_et_from_schedule come from the official schedule PDF (LOCAL/ET columns) and the nba.com games pages, which print AM/PM.

Rows that continue across a PDF page break lose their Game Date, Game Time and sometimes Team cells. Where a player row's team cell was lost, the team cell is stored as "__lost__" and flagged; no team is repaired from another document (policy P5-02).

7 player rows lost their team cell at a page break (5 in MEM@WAS between the printed Memphis rows and the Washington NOT YET SUBMITTED row; 2 in GSW@NOP after the printed New Orleans Pelicans rows). They are stored with team "__lost__" and an explanatory flag.

The 6 Golden State Warriors rows of GSW@NOP extract with 6 cells only: the Reason column is absent for the whole sub-block. Reasons are left blank and the rows are flagged. The Butler III row's single status-position cell holds reason-formatted text and is reproduced verbatim in the status field with no status asserted.

The ORL@BOS block's player rows and the POR@MIN 11/16 block's rows extract with blank date and/or time cells (page-break context). Game date/tip for those blocks are recorded from the block context and marked cells_source "report-context"; the schedule PDF rows 245 and 250 corroborate the date and tip.

The 11/17 tail blocks (DET@SAS, POR@MIN, UTA@LAC, CHA@LAL) print their time and matchup cells but the date cell is blank; the date 2026-11-17 comes from the preceding NYK@TOR block header and is corroborated by schedule rows 253-257 (cells_source "report-context").

A team that has not filed shows an empty player/status pair with the reason NOT YET SUBMITTED. That is a reporting state, not an absence of injuries, and no status may be inferred from it. On the page-5 rows the marker extracts in a collapsed 5-cell layout; it is stored in the reason field per the established convention.

Two 11/17 tips disagree with the August schedule PDF: UTA@LAC prints 10:30 (ET) here (schedule row 257 prints 11:00 PM ET) and CHA@LAL prints 11:00 (ET) (schedule row 256 prints 10:00 PM ET). The nba.com games pages print 10:30 PM ET and 11:00 PM ET respectively, agreeing with this report against the schedule PDF. Both readings are kept as printed and flagged (board flag AN-02, review flag P9-03).

The POR@MIN matchup code appears twice in this report: once for the 11/16 game (player rows, schedule row 250) and once for the 11/17 game (NOT YET SUBMITTED rows, schedule row 254). Rows are matched to games by (date, code), never by code alone.

The 13 matchup codes printed in this report (8 games on 11/16, 5 games on 11/17) match schedule rows 245-257 one-for-one and corroborate the away/home order shown on the slate page. The report does not list 11/18 games (schedule rows 258-269).
No availability probability, minute estimate or production impact is stored here or derived from these rows.

matchups_not_in_snapshot.note: the 09:15 AM report does not list 11/18 games; scheduled reporting deadlines make those reports later. The codes above follow the schedule PDF rows 258-269; rows 260-269 print an explicit 'at' token (away team first) and rows 258-259 are corroborated by the nba.com games page slugs mem-vs-cle and hou-vs-ind.
